primary_bridge.short_exact_quote: Naikṛi (Nk.), a dialect of Kolami (= LSI, Bhili of Basim).
primary_bridge.interpretation: Section 27 explicitly equates the historical Basim label with Naikri. Section 28 treats Naiki of Chanda separately; this supports the current distinct canonical routes.

original_context.finding: Kolami/Basim/Chanda are grouped as Dravidian varieties, not as ordinary Indo-Aryan Bhili.
Page is shared: upper text continues Kolami specimen 75; the Basim subsection starts below a horizontal rule. Its running header is not a page-wide language attribution.
The demographic Bhil total does not prove that all Bhils in Pusad/Basim speak this dialect. The actual received Basim specimen is explicitly compared with Kolami.
Specimen 76 explicitly identifies the Dravidian-family so-called Bhili of district Basim.

historical_record.reason: Original p566 explicitly says Bhili received from Basim and compares it with Kolami; the n/nd/d forms are that witness, not Parji. Nordic page metadata proposes Southwestern Kolami-Washim (nit), whereas existing Kolami is nort2699 and Naiki is naik1250. Neither existing base nor a northern Kolami locality is securely interchangeable. Preserve all five records under unresolved historical Bhili of Basim pending an approved identity route; never Parji or Indo-Aryan Bhili.
